subject: UK IDTA addendum, SCCs compatibility & subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Clare Hughes <clare.hughes@arktech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2027 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: UK IDTA addendum / SCCs compatibility — next steps

Hi Clare —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per ArkTech's legal team's request, we took another pass on the DPA to surface a UK IDTA addendum and confirm compatibility with the EU SCCs your procurement team needs. Attached is our proposed redline (redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx) and a short SCCs compatibility note.

Key asks from our side:
- Can you confirm a single point of contact for the ArkTech side to receive subprocessor notifications (name + ops email)?
- Would ArkTech accept our proposed fallback language that relies on SCCs + documented transfer impact assessment rather than adding broad additional transfer restrictions in the body of the IDTA?

We'd like to get to an agreed mark to put into DocuSign by next week if possible. Rishi — tagging you for suggested language on subprocessor evidence and the transfer-impact statement. Marissa/Monica — please keep me posted on timelines for evidence upload if ArkTech requires SOC2 artifacts.

Attachments: redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: Clare Hughes <clare.hughes@arktech.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@arktech.com
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2027 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: UK IDTA addendum / SCCs compatibility — next steps

Laura —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Quick answers:
- Point of contact: Contracts team (contracts@arktech.com). For operational notifications we'd prefer an ops email (ops-notify@arktech.com) — I'll confirm a primary name tomorrow.
- Transfer approach: Our security team prefers a clear commitment in the IDTA/addendum that we can rely on; the SCCs alone are often fine but procurement needs an explicit UK IDTA statement that aligns with our internal policy.

Two items from ArkTech: we inserted two counter-redlines to tighten subprocessor onboarding notice periods and to require evidence for subprocessors processing EU/UK user data (see attached arktech_counter-redlines.docx). We can be flexible on wording but need assurance that evidence (SOC2 report or equivalent) will be available within 10 business days upon request.

Will loop in our security lead if there are technical questions on the SCCs assessment.

Best,
Clare Hughes
Senior Counsel, Commercial
ArkTech Systems
clare.hughes@arktech.com

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: UK IDTA addendum / SCCs compatibility — next steps

Clare/Laura —

Thanks for the quick review, Clare. We've reviewed ArkTech's counter-redlines and propose the following compromise to address the evidence/timing ask without changing our subprocessor cadence:

1) Subprocessor evidence clause (proposed paragraph):
"Upon receipt of a written request from Customer, Redwood will make available within 10 business days relevant third-party audit reports (e.g., SOC 2 Type II) or equivalent compliance evidence for any Subprocessor that processes Customer Personal Data in the EU or UK; where such evidence is unavailable Redwood will provide a summary of compensating controls and a remediation plan."

2) Transfer-impact statement (to live in the UK addendum):
"To the extent transfers of Personal Data from the UK to a jurisdiction outside the UK rely on the Standard Contractual Clauses (or valid alternative mechanisms), Redwood will maintain a documented Transfer Impact Assessment and operational controls consistent with the SCCs’ requirements and will provide a redacted summary to Customer upon request."

We attach a short SCCs assessment summary that maps our current posture to the Article-by-Article SCCs expectations (sccs-assessment-summary.pdf). Note: the assessment contains redacted infrastructure details; production artifacts (SOC2 report) are held in our secure evidence workspace per our contract with auditors.

If ArkTech requires the full SOC2 report in-cabinet rather than evidence-on-request we need to discuss scope and an NDA with our auditors — that will take longer.

Happy to take a 30-minute call to walk through the assessment next week.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Compliance & Privacy
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Clare Hughes <clare.hughes@arktech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@arktech.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: UK IDTA addendum / SCCs compatibility — next steps

Rishi/Laura —

Thanks for the language and the SCCs summary. That proposed subprocessor evidence paragraph gets close to what our procurement team needs. A couple of follow-ups:

- We need the 10-business-day window to be explicitly calendar/business (your text says "business" which is fine) and to include a point of escalation if evidence cannot be provided in time. Could we add: "Customer may escalate to customer.contracts@arktech.com and request a senior compliance contact at Redwood for exceptional cases"?
- For the transfer-impact statement we want the redacted TIA summary to include a statement on whether any onward transfers to subprocessors located in third countries occur and whether SCCs cover those transfers.

If you can accept those additions we'll route the combined mark to our CPO for sign-off and then to procurement for DocuSign. We prefer DocuSign for EU/UK signings.

Clare

Clare —

We can accept the escalation line you proposed. Updated suggested sentence for clarity: 
"If Redwood is unable to provide the requested evidence within 10 business days, Customer may escalate to customer.contracts@arktech.com and request escalation to Redwood's senior compliance contact, who will propose a remediation or interim evidence path within 5 business days of escalation."

On the TIA summary, we will include explicit confirmation about onward transfers to subprocessors and whether SCCs or equivalent mechanisms cover them (redacted as needed). I will ask our compliance team to add that paragraph to the TIA summary — Rishi, can your team produce that redacted line and attach to the DocuSign packet?

- Rishi to drop updated clause and TIA redaction (internal) by EOD tomorrow.
- Laura to send the combined mark and DocuSign envelope link to ArkTech contracts once we have the confirmation.
- Marissa/Monica prepare a secure evidence share for SOC2 if ArkTech requests the full report.

Once ArkTech's CPO signs, we'll execute via DocuSign and follow the evidence onboarding checklist.

Thanks all — moving to execution.
